news.headline: WGS stock slips after report of softer full-year test volume
news.summary: GeneDx shares fell after commentary signaling softer full-year exome and genome test volume than previously modeled. It reinforced the demand and reimbursement concerns first flagged with the Q1 miss and is the freshest operational read heading into the Q2 print.

news.headline: Piper Sandler raises GeneDx price target to $63 from $50, keeps Overweight
news.summary: Piper Sandler lifted its target to $63 and reiterated Overweight after Carelon codified outpatient genome coverage, calling it a structural ASP de-risking event. The firm estimates the policy could add roughly $100 of incremental average selling price by H2 2027 as the exome-to-genome mix shifts.

news.headline: GeneDx names Mark Gardner President to lead its next phase of scale and growth
news.summary: GeneDx appointed Mark Gardner, former SVP of Molecular Genomics and Oncology at Quest Diagnostics and ex-CEO of OmniSeq, as President effective June 15, reporting to CEO Katherine Stueland. He takes over commercial and operations, signaling a sharpened focus on execution at scale amid the guidance reset.

news.headline: Carelon adds outpatient genome sequencing coverage, lifting insured coverage toward ~80%
news.summary: Carelon, a large U.S. lab benefit manager, added genome sequencing under the same clinical criteria as exome for undiagnosed rare disease, raising insured genome coverage toward ~80%. It is a structural volume and reimbursement tailwind and arguably the most important positive development of the period, underpinning the view that the sell-off went too far.

news.headline: Hedge funder Eli Casdin keeps loading up on GeneDx shares
news.summary: Casdin Capital added roughly $32M of GeneDx stock across May and June open-market buys, lifting its stake to about 3.7 million shares. The board-linked, ~10% holder's accumulation into the crash reads as a contrarian vote of confidence.

news.headline: GeneDx reports Q1 2026, cuts full-year outlook on Fabric Genomics impairment
news.summary: GeneDx posted Q1 revenue of ~$102M with exome/genome volume up ~34% YoY, but took a ~$31M impairment tied to the Fabric Genomics acquisition, saw adjusted gross margin slip to ~69%, and cut FY2026 revenue guidance to roughly $475-490M. Shares fell about 49% the next day, the defining event driving current sentiment.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: First print under the reset guidance, expected late July/early August. Company guided to $110-112M revenue, ~30,000 exome/genome tests, ~70% adjusted gross margin and a ~$5M adjusted net loss. Key credibility test on volume trends and whether the reimbursement/Fabric weakness stabilizes.

catalysts.label: Genome ASP uplift from coverage
catalysts.detail: Carelon's genome coverage decision plus further payer and Medicaid wins could lift genome volume and average selling price. Piper Sandler estimates roughly $100 of incremental ASP by H2 2027 as the exome-to-genome mix shifts.

catalysts.label: FY2026 guidance delivery
catalysts.detail: Management targets roughly $475-490M revenue with continued 30%+ exome/genome volume growth and ~70% adjusted gross margin. Delivering on the lowered bar is the near-term thesis anchor after the May reset.

catalysts.label: New President ramp / health-system expansion
catalysts.detail: Mark Gardner's arrival puts commercial and operations under a seasoned diagnostics operator; watch for improved sales productivity, expanded Epic (Aura) EHR integration and newborn genomic screening rollouts.

pulse: GeneDx remains a high-volatility, headline-driven name still digesting its May Q1 report, where a ~$31M Fabric Genomics impairment, softer reimbursement and a full-year revenue guidance cut to ~$475-490M drove a ~49% crash; a July 10 signal of lighter full-year test volume added fresh pressure. The bull case rests on structural reimbursement wins - Carelon lifted insured genome coverage toward ~80% and Piper Sandler raised its target to $63 citing ASP de-risking - plus ~34% exome/genome volume growth and open-market accumulation by ~10% holder Eli Casdin. New President Mark Gardner is charged with restoring execution credibility ahead of the early-August Q2 print, the next key proof point.
